full_judgment:
Abu Sayeed Ahmmed J: Defendant-petitioner seeks leave to appeal calling in question the judgment and order dated 25-7-2001 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3696 of 1999 discharging the Rule and upholding the judgment and decree dated 22-6-1999 passed by the 3rd Court of the Subordinate Judge (Small Cause Court), Dhaka in SCC Suit No. 4 of 1997 decreeing the suit for ejectment against the petitioner as monthly tenant and in favour of the respondent who filed the suit as landlord. 

 6. Said title suit and the SCC suit both were heard analogously. The SCC suit was decreed and the title suit was dismissed by the judgment and decree of the trial Court. 

 7. Against the judgment and decree passed in the suit for ejectment, the defendant-petitioner obtained the Rule from the High Court Division wherein he also pleaded the same contention that he was in possession of the disputed premises as its owner upon purchase and, as such, there is no question of default in payment of rent by the petitioner of the disputed premises to the respondent. 

 "This Rule arises out of a simple suit for ejectment of a monthly tenant on the ground of default in the payment of rent and also bonafide requirement of the premises for the purpose of construction. It is not disputed (that the defendant entered into the premises as a monthly tenant. Case of the defendant is that he entered in 1972 while case of the plaintiff is that he took lease with effect from 1 May, 1987. This does not matter much when admittedly the defendant entered into the premises as a monthly lessee and, in law, he will continue as such till he surrenders possession of the premises to the landlord vacating the premises. Plaintiff adduced number of rent receipts showing payment of rents and also letter Ext. 'Nio' by which defendant requested for monthly lease. Rent receipts are marked as Ext. 'Ta' series and 'To'. The defence is that the defendant since 1987 is possessing the premise on his own right on the basis of an agreement for sale of the premises. No agreement could be produced as found by the trial Court. Defendant has also failed to prove his contract. So, the case of the plaintiff is established that defendant is occupying the premises as an unauthorised occupant after valid termination of the lease with effect from 28-2-1997. Plaintiff also proved bonafide requirement by adducing the plan as sanctioned by RAJUK Ext. 'Cha'. The judgment and decree of the trial Court for ejectment on the ground of default in the payment of rent and bona fide requirement are borne out by the evidence, oral and documentary, on record and therefore, do not call for any interference by this Division. It may be noted that in the circumstances the law is settled that the moment a tenant denies the title of his landlord he forfeits his right to stay in the premises. In the case of Haji Easimuddin Mandal vs Md Jalaluddin Pramanik 48 DLR (AD) 205, our Appellate Division held that a tenant cannot set up title to a property of which he is a monthly tenant without surrendering possession to his landlord."
